approach.method_basis: The Parent trains a recurrent SMILES language model on an unlabeled molecular corpus and starts each objective with a fresh policy copied from that frozen prior. Each accepted batch supplies its highest-scoring half, joined by the strongest eligible original strings from a memory of thirty-two earlier elites. Historical fitting weights decrease with previous training exposure while current and historical groups retain their total loss shares. The policy fits weighted squared error toward frozen-prior sequence log likelihood plus sixty times accepted reward, projecting each positive target independently to zero, using bounded clipped Adam updates and retaining the final policy. It then samples complete SMILES directly from the adapted policy and submits the first valid, canonically novel identities in sample order, refilling when necessary and discarding surplus draws.
approach.novelty: Add progressive spacing of repeated molecular cores during admission. The first new molecule with a ring-and-linker core is admitted immediately. Once that core occupies k places in the current batch, its next admission requires k+1 further distinct valid draws of that core; intervening draws are discarded. Other newly encountered cores can therefore reach the same batch, while a dominant core remains admissible and no randomness is added. Earlier siblings diversified retained training memory or balanced choices of breeding parents. This change acts directly on fresh policy samples before oracle submission, leaving both training membership rules and token generation intact. Same-stream admission receipts will show whether additional cores actually reach evaluation. The earlier diversity experiments also warn that spacing a productive family can weaken exploitation.

hypothesis: Deterministically thin repeated atom/bond-typed Murcko cores within each suggestion: after k molecules of a core have been emitted, admit its next member only on the (k+1)-th distinct valid canonical-novel draw of that core since its preceding emission, resetting that per-core interval after admission; first occurrences and identity-keyed acyclic or extraction-fallback draws pass immediately.

finding_summary.headline: Core thinning delivered broader molecular batches, but final Top-1 fell despite higher AUC.
finding_summary.insights:
The experiment resolves the delivery question: additional cores already present in fresh policy samples can reach the oracle without losing the first-come batch's core support. That delivery was often unproductive. Of the 242 additional core representatives, only six improved the actual incumbent: four on zaleplon and two on docking. Deco-hop received 116 additional core representatives without an incumbent improvement from any of them. Its previously dominant phenyl/anilinoquinazoline core was evaluated 54 times instead of 160 and reached a lower best score. This is compatible with diluted exploitation, although unscored discarded molecules cannot identify the value of any particular forgone proposal.

Coverage is also a poor predictor of the magnitude of the final change. Sitagliptin gained only seven batch-level cores yet had the largest mean endpoint loss. Admission changes alter later feedback and therefore later generated streams; a same-stream comparison isolates immediate delivery, not the complete search that would have followed different admissions. The higher AUC and lower endpoint further separate earlier progress from the final objective.

The chemical assessment narrows what broader coverage did not repair. Productive functional-group attachment arrangements remain inconsistently preserved, and the many structures with potential stereochemistry still have no specified configurations. Those are open chemical capabilities, not established causes of this score loss. Useful next evidence would need to show that broader admission preserves productive local series or transfers their attachment chemistry, rather than using core count as a proxy for usefulness. The utility claim is rejected while the admission and delivery mechanism is confirmed.
finding_summary.results:
The admission mechanism ran correctly and changed which constitutional cores reached evaluation. Across 435 batches, it rejected 436 eligible repeated-core draws in 167 batches. Comparing each recorded stream with its first ten valid novel structures, actual batches gained cores 159 times and never lost a previously represented core. Mean core count increased from 9.106 to 9.662, delivering 242 additional batch-level core representatives and changing 304 canonical output identities. Mean core concentration fell from 0.133 to 0.110. All state transitions, original-string provenance and paired behavior before the first intervention passed the passive audit.

All fifteen task sessions completed their budgets. Mean final Top-1 fell from 0.522705 to 0.508247, a paired change of -0.014458 against the required +0.002 increase. Seed changes were +0.009826, -0.032176 and -0.021023; population dispersion across seed scores changed from 0.020072 to 0.019593. Task mean changes were -0.014692 for zaleplon, -0.014459 for deco-hop, -0.005454 for median-2 and -0.037685 for sitagliptin; docking decreased by only 0.000000211 near its ceiling. Recorded mean AUC nevertheless rose from 0.405593 to 0.430066, chiefly through earlier progress on docking and zaleplon.

Broader batches required more work. Raw draws increased from 35,568 to 36,880, and batches needing extra sampling increased from 16 to 28. Raw duplication rose from 32.21% to 34.50%, while validity fell from 91.79% to 91.11%. No generation limit was exhausted. Recorded generation time rose from 24.75 to 37.90 seconds across the panel, including 10.38 seconds for core extraction and 0.52 seconds for receipts; the interval gate itself took 0.009 seconds.

molecular.headline: Broad aromatic and heterocyclic chemistry, but undefined stereochemistry and uneven preservation of productive functional-group arrangements.
molecular.overall_character:
Node n-33f9aab34e21 produces recognizable medicinal-chemistry families: fused azaaromatics and indoles bearing amides or carbamates, decorated anilinoquinazolines, arylpiperazines and other saturated ring amines, and arylsulfonylpiperazines. It also produces long-chain, peptide-like, unusually connected and highly elaborated polycyclic structures. Across the five covered tasks, each digest contains 900 accepted records, including 870 optimizer proposals across seeds 0, 1 and 2. Ring-closure text rates range from 0.9816 to 0.9966 and aromatic-atom text rates from 0.9379 to 0.9943; these are molecule-presence counters, not fractions of atoms or RDKit ring counts. Halogen text rates range from 0.3161 to 0.8. The global output is constitutionally broad.

The passive RDKit 2023.09.6 audit reads all 30 supplied child and Parent trajectories, totaling 9,000 accepted records. Every child optimizer record parses, which establishes accepted-structure validity rather than raw-generation validity or makeability. Child median heavy-atom counts in the fixed task order are 24, 33, 28, 23.5 and 24; median perceived ring counts are 3, 4, 4, 3 and 3. Distinct atom/bond-typed Murcko keys, with each acyclic identity counted independently, are 577, 473, 626, 749 and 792, versus Parent counts 542, 360, 598, 740 and 791. These are full-panel constitutional coverage measurements, not evidence about admission activation or utility. The diverse global inventory coexists with much narrower families among the digest best molecules.

All five digest stereocentre text rates are zero. The structural audit finds potential tetrahedral centres in 1,159 of the 4,350 child optimizer appearances, with no assigned centres; 722 appearances have potential double-bond stereochemistry, with none specified. Counts are appearances across independent sessions, not distinct compounds. The Parent also has no assigned centres. Saturated and bridged ring construction therefore does not establish stereochemical definition. The ordinary aryl-amide, heteroaryl and piperazine members look synthetically plausible at the motif level, while unusual neutral sulfur valence, small imine rings, N-N/N-O arrangements and complex unassigned polycycles make the overall makeability judgement mixed. No synthesis route, isolated stereoisomer, biological activity or score causality is established by these records. The audit and its exact digest witnesses are recorded in runs/SPIRAL2/policy/responses/r0012-02-improve-L03-molecular.audit.json, generated by the adjacent .audit.py. All five objectives have trajectories; none is omitted.

per_task.generated_character: The proposals are predominantly compact aromatic amides and carbamates, with indole/other fused azaaromatic cores, pendant phenyl or pyridyl groups, and occasional partly saturated heterocycles. Median size is 24 heavy atoms and 3 rings; 593 optimizer appearances contain an amide substructure. The digest best molecules have 23-26 heavy atoms and 3-4 rings. The best, an acetamidoindole bearing a phenyl-substituted isoxazoline, scores 0.48839749189747395 and has an unspecified tetrahedral centre. Other strong examples are an acrylamido methoxyanilinoquinoline and alkynyl or allyl carbamates on a phenyl-substituted fused diazole. Their ordinary aromatic amide chemistry is plausible; the smaller imine-ring and oxygen-rich ring variants deserve individual synthetic assessment. In contrast, the low end includes long hydrocarbon chains, an extensively substituted polycyclic lactone/acid, and a large multiaryl sulfonamide. Relative to the Parent, the accepted inventory has more core keys, 577 versus 542, and more appearances with potential unassigned centres, 167 versus 86, while its median size stays 24 heavy atoms.
liabilities: Large hydrocarbon appendages and crowded multiaryl or polycyclic structures broaden size and conformational burden well beyond the compact high-score examples.

Acrylamides and other conjugated carbonyls, N-O heterocycles and the small imine-ring analogue require contextual reactivity and synthesis assessment; their presence is not itself evidence of an invalid or low-scoring molecule.
missing_features: Many weak proposals fail to retain the compact placement of carbonyl-linked nitrogen and fused aromatic donor/acceptor sites present in the best examples. These groups are demonstrably producible; their productive arrangement is inconsistently preserved during growth or scaffold changes.

The isoxazoline family supplies tetrahedral shape without specifying its configuration. The records do not test whether stereochemical definition changes this objective, and they do not identify a unique absent target ring or substituent.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The gradient supports compact composition and precise carbonyl/heteroaromatic attachment rather than ring count alone. Moving the acetamide around the same indole/isoxazoline family gives 0.48839749189747395 versus 0.4767312946227961. On the shared fused-diazole carbamate, the methyl-extended alkynyl group scores 0.4546547989309981, the allyl group 0.4226489847472999, and the terminal-alkyne variant in the final excerpt 0.33748438760743243. These are local associations, not independent effects of unsaturation. The initial trimethoxyindole carboxanilide scores 0.3051048083696145. Elaborating an otherwise related aromatic carbonyl compound with a long dicarbonyl chain gives 1.978240337577409e-21, while the 49-heavy-atom multiaryl sulfonamide scores 1.2150684990266398e-23. The final simple diaryl thioamide scores 0.0002269799216711376. Parent terminal best-so-far values were 0.43351949803907636, 0.4767312946227961 and 0.5; child values are 0.48839749189747395, 0.42312329948394145 and 0.4546547989309981. The changed chemistry accompanies mixed seed outcomes.

per_task.generated_character: This is the largest and most aromatic proposal set: median 33 heavy atoms, 4 perceived aromatic rings, and a halogen text rate of 0.8. The pooled digest best molecules all come from seed 2 and are dimethoxy anilinoquinazolines with fluorinated aniline substituents and phenyl, pyridyl or thiophenyl arms. Their sizes are 28-34 heavy atoms; most have 4 aromatic rings, with one additional cyclobutane in an elaborated analogue. These are recognizable heteroaryl coupling/amination motifs, though the many aromatic rings and halogenated appendages merit physical-property scrutiny. The full trajectories also include nitro-rich hydrazone/heteroaryl families and fluorinated triaryltriazines in the other seeds; the best excerpt is not representative of every seed. The child has 473 core keys versus the Parent's 360, and its largest exact core appears 62 times versus 160. Quinazoline-containing appearances are 221 versus 341, so broader constitutional coverage coexists with strong local family recurrence.
liabilities: Substantial aromatic and halogen loading and occasional long or bulky appendages create plausible solubility and conformational liabilities; no measured solubility is supplied.

Nitro-rich hydrazones in other seeds and unusual N-N/N-O-containing structures require more synthetic and stability scrutiny than the ordinary anilinoquinazoline members. RDKit parsing alone cannot distinguish those cases.
missing_features: The best excerpt explores aryl identity and fluorination around a persistent dimethoxy/anilino attachment pattern much more than alternative alkoxy arrangements. More extensive alkoxy decoration occurs in the Parent's strong family but is absent from this best excerpt; its causal benefit is untested.

Weak aromatic proposals often lack the particular donor/acceptor and substituent geometry retained in the strong anilinoquinazolines. Aromaticity is already abundant, and the records do not establish a missing universal heterocycle or basic amine requirement.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The best pyridyl/difluoroanilino member scores 0.6462372658560631, versus 0.6457672152926415 for its phenyl analogue; adding a further aniline fluorine gives 0.6460892049127344. These differences do not support a simple more-halogen rule. Low-score molecules remain aromatic and often similarly sized, but rearrange the heteroaromatic/linker pattern or introduce sulfone-rich extensions: the benzodioxole/sulfone/unsaturated ester scores 0.2948214550303749, and an elaborated 46-heavy-atom quinazoline with a benzylsulfone extension scores 0.3716299019607843. The final seven-membered cyclic-amine substitution on a related quinazoline scores 0.6061725138485887. The Parent's strongest seed-2 family included more extensive alkoxy decoration and reached 0.6669492630755185; the child reaches 0.6462372658560631. The other child seed endpoints, 0.588961510530138 and 0.6146044624746451, also sit below the corresponding Parent records. Extra accepted core variety does not by itself identify a better chemical answer.

per_task.generated_character: The strong molecules are aromatic anchors joined to nonacylated aliphatic amines, especially arylpiperazines with benzyl/phenylalkyl substituents, and phenolic fused-ring amines joined through alkyl diamine chains. The digest best molecules have 23-31 heavy atoms and 3-4 rings, combining 2-3 aromatic rings with saturated nitrogen rings. Methoxy, thioether, nitrile, fluorine and methyl substituents decorate these families. The full proposal median is 28 heavy atoms and 4 rings. A conservative structural proxy finds a nonaromatic, nonconjugated amine site in 587 optimizer appearances versus 530 in the Parent, and piperazine occurs in 220 versus 201. Basic ring-amine chemistry is therefore plainly present. Parent and child strong families overlap chemically, while later child examples also include bridged phenolic amines and an unusual neutral hydrogen-bearing sulfur ring. Ordinary arylpiperazines are plausible medicinal structures; the complex bridged and unusual sulfur members are less straightforward.
liabilities: Several strong members combine multiple aromatic surfaces with long flexible alkyl chains and multiple amine sites. Those features imply possible physical-property and conformational liabilities that a nearly saturated recorded score does not characterize.

The final sulfur-containing ring has an unusual neutral sulfur bonding pattern, and the more intricate bridged amines leave multiple centres undefined. They should not inherit a makeability claim from the simpler piperazine series.
missing_features: Some low-score ring-containing molecules lack the nonacylated aliphatic amine/aryl attachment context recurrent among the strong molecules, even when they contain a saturated nitrogen ring. This is an attachment-chemistry gap in part of the output, not a generator-wide absence of amines.

The branched and bridged proposals lack assigned stereochemistry. Potential tetrahedral centres occur in 435 child appearances versus 192 in the Parent, with none assigned in either. No score experiment here establishes a stereochemical benefit.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The methoxy-substituted biphenyl/piperazine/phenylpropyl molecule and its methylthio counterpart both score 0.9999998674084429, and the branched pyridylalkyl piperazine scores 0.9999998517131371. High scores tolerate considerable aromatic decoration and linker variation around exposed aliphatic amine sites. A low-score heteroarylamide still contains a piperidine ring, but its nitrogen is directly sulfonylated; it scores 1.9828327575562915e-05. The acidic nitro-heteroaromatic amide scores 1.8588450134335675e-05. Counting ring nitrogens without their bonding context misses the observed separation. These are structural associations, not measured pKa values, docking contacts or experimental activity. The final phenolic ring amine scores 0.9971900592268141, whereas the unusual sulfur-ring proposal scores 0.31554657771518013; they are not a matched molecular pair. Parent and child seed endpoints are all already very near the numerical ceiling, so the records cannot resolve a new required pharmacophore.

per_task.generated_character: The stronger output is dominated by arylsulfonylpiperazines: naphthylsulfonyl groups on N-methyl/N-ethyl/N-propyl piperazine, and benzodioxane or benzodioxepine arylsulfonyl groups on arylpiperazines. These combine saturated diaza rings, aromatic surfaces, sulfonyl oxygen acceptors and, in some members, ring ethers. Most digest best examples have 20-28 heavy atoms and 3-4 rings; a larger 38-heavy-atom heterocyclic example also appears. Median proposal size is 23.5 heavy atoms and 3 rings. The conventional sulfonylation and N-substitution motifs look plausible; some oxime/hydrazone and polycyclic departures are less straightforward. The full child inventory is broad, with 749 core keys versus 740 in the Parent. Nevertheless, piperazine appearances are 186 versus 231 and sulfonylpiperazine appearances 82 versus 102.
liabilities: Small azide and unusual N-hydroxy/trichloromethyl fragments are chemically unlike the ordinary sulfonylpiperazine series and need separate handling and synthetic assessment.
Some final alternatives add hydrazone/oxime bonds or complicated unassigned polycycles. They expand structures without demonstrating that the strong series' functional arrangement has been retained.
missing_features: Weak fragments and rearranged piperazine/oxime proposals often omit the sulfonyl-linked aromatic and diaza-ring relationship seen near the top. Sulfur, aromaticity or a cyclic amine alone does not reproduce the supported arrangement.

The modest strong-series scores and narrow N-substitution/aryl-position changes do not establish a unique absent bridging group or target scaffold. The observable shortfall is incomplete retention and exploration of the whole successful attachment pattern, despite broad unrelated core coverage.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The N-methyl naphthylsulfonylpiperazine scores 0.23735633163877068, compared with 0.207375126170294 for N-ethyl and 0.20874143036171652 for N-propyl. Alkyl growth is not monotonically rewarded. The benzodioxane-sulfonyl arylpiperazine scores 0.21430090054520579, and its ortho-chloro analogue 0.21766212246744293. A bis-sulfonylpiperazine still scores 0.20796528955536797 despite lacking the ordinary free amine environment of the N-methyl member. The common association is the assembled aryl-sulfonyl/diaza-ring topology rather than a universal basicity requirement. Weak examples include the acyclic allyl azide at 0.0, N-hydroxy trichloromethyl formamide at 0.007693218186208301 and urea at 0.008404548427654986. A final tolyl N-methylpiperazine without the sulfonyl-linked aromatic component scores 0.14832850691857688. Parent versus child endpoint records are 0.2125118592516207 versus 0.21766212246744293, 0.20428349275442803 versus the same value, and 0.2588686674995393 versus 0.23735633163877068. The best seed-2 family changes from a more elaborate bis-sulfonyl arrangement in the Parent to a simpler naphthyl sulfonamide in the child.

per_task.generated_character: This output is constitutionally dispersed rather than trapped in one scaffold: 792 core keys among 870 optimizer appearances, compared with 791 in the Parent. Median size is 24 heavy atoms and 3 rings. The best molecule is a fluorinated anilide connected through a branched chain to an oxalamide, with 26 heavy atoms, one aromatic ring and an unassigned tetrahedral centre. The next is an N-sulfonyl imidazoline carrying fluorophenyl and methyl-benzoate groups, with 25 heavy atoms and 3 rings. Other strong examples include a guanidino/amino-substituted tetrahydroisoquinoline, compact oxygen/nitrogen ring systems, and nitrogen-rich heteroaromatic carbonyl compounds. Ordinary amide and sulfonamide motifs are plausible, but the more intricate ring connections require individual synthetic assessment. The low end includes multiaryl hydrophobes, long-chain thioether esters, and large peptide-like structures. Potential unassigned tetrahedral centres occur in 288 child appearances versus 274 in the Parent.
liabilities: Large peptide-like structures and long hydrocarbon-rich appendages occupy opposite extremes of polarity and flexibility, while both can have negligible recorded scores.

Acylated nitrogens, guanidines, cyclic amidines, thioureas, oximes and nitro heterocycles have different bonding and likely ionization/reactivity contexts. Treating their nitrogen counts as interchangeable would obscure the chemistry, and no measured ionization or stability data are supplied.
missing_features: Many proposals contain fluorinated aryl groups, nitrogen or carbonyls separately without the compact connected polar architecture shown in the stronger examples. The widely different strong scaffolds do not reveal a unique missing target-specific motif.

The best branched anilide and several fused or bridged examples lack specified configuration. Primary aliphatic amino substructures occur in 24 appearances, so total absence of that functionality would be a false diagnosis; its useful attachment context and any stereochemical score dependence remain unresolved.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The branched fluoroanilide/oxalamide scores 0.3085499097640706, the fluorophenyl sulfonylimidazoline 0.3034617343186778, and the nonfluorinated guanidino fused-ring molecule 0.2711448282680827. These examples support moderate size with specific nitrogen/carbonyl/aryl arrangements, but do not isolate fluorination, a free primary amine or one ring class as necessary. Adding fluorines to the sulfonylimidazoline/benzoate family gives 0.18136420222115457, below the less fluorinated member. The low digest examples include a 47-heavy-atom multiaryl structure and a 61-heavy-atom peptide-like structure, both at 0.0; simply adding aromatic or polar material is insufficient. Final fluorinated, heteroatom-rich structures can also be weak: the diaryl pyrazole carboxamide scores 0.00017370401130919412. The reported digest median is 0.0; this rounded summary is not a count of exact-zero records. The Parent's best seed-2 fluoroaryl N-sulfonylamide had a secondary aminoacetyl chain and scored 0.32609684308650033, whereas the child's best anilide/oxalamide has acylated nitrogens and scores 0.3085499097640706. This is a changed polar-linker arrangement, not an isolated amine comparison. Seed 0 retains the same 0.2711448282680827 guanidino structure; seed 1 changes from a carbonyl/thioamide-rich family at 0.26424211308214746 to a heteroaryl thiourea/piperazine at 0.16873483388608349.

transferable_gaps.evidence: All five supplied stereocentre text rates are zero. Passive perception finds potential tetrahedral centres in 1,159 of 4,350 optimizer appearances and potential double-bond stereochemistry in 722, with no specified instances. The digest includes unassigned centres in strong isoxazoline, branched arylalkylpiperazine, fused-ring amine and branched anilide examples. These are observed representation omissions, not demonstrated explanations for score shortfalls.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator emits many stereogenic structures but shows no ability to specify their configurations.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: A task-agnostic generator would need to represent and vary configuration where the generated graph permits it, preserving full molecular identity and letting its own accepted feedback establish usefulness. Additional ring cores or saturated atoms alone do not supply this capability.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Aryl-linked, nonacylated ring amines occur among digest molecules scoring 0.9999998674084429, while a ring nitrogen directly sulfonylated in a heteroarylamide occurs at 1.9828327575562915e-05. In a different supplied score context, an arylsulfonylpiperazine scores 0.23735633163877068 and a bis-sulfonylpiperazine remains at 0.20796528955536797. These comparisons have multiple structural differences; they show why neither adding nitrogen nor globally avoiding sulfonamides is an adequate chemical prescription.
transferable_gaps.gap: The output does not consistently preserve the attachment context that makes its amine, carbonyl and sulfonyl motifs chemically distinct.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: The generator would need to learn connected functional-group environments and support modifications that keep a rewarded ring/linker arrangement while varying nearby functionality. Whether nitrogen is aliphatic, aryl-bound, acylated or sulfonylated must remain visible to that task-local learning; no particular amine or sulfur motif should be imposed across objectives.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Compact best examples include 23-26-heavy-atom fused aromatic carbonyl compounds and 18-28-heavy-atom nitrogen/carbonyl-rich compounds. The supplied low-score witnesses include a 49-heavy-atom multiaryl sulfonamide at 1.2150684990266398e-23 and a 61-heavy-atom peptide-like structure at 0.0, while small acyclic urea and unusual N-hydroxy fragments are also weak in their own score contexts. Size is not sufficient: similarly sized aromatic sulfone and anilinoheterocycle structures also differ substantially in recorded score.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator lacks consistent local control over growth and truncation around its productive molecular families.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: A task-agnostic generator would need to preserve locally supported size and connected polar/aromatic arrangements while exploring controlled growth, shortening and linker changes. Local accepted evidence should determine useful ranges; a universal size cutoff or extra heteroatom rule would discard the distinction visible in these molecules.

transferable_gaps.evidence: One supplied panel expands from 360 Parent core keys to 473 child keys, yet all twelve digest best examples retain a dimethoxy anilinoquinazoline pattern while largely varying aryl identity and halogen decoration. A stronger Parent member in that family had a different, more extensive alkoxy arrangement. Another panel has 749 child keys but only 82 sulfonylpiperazine appearances versus 102 in the Parent. These are accepted-output associations, not proof that any discarded or ungenerated molecule would improve a score.
transferable_gaps.gap: Broad constitutional output is not accompanied by equally broad preservation and variation of productive peripheral chemistry.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: The generator would need support for transferring and varying peripheral functional groups and their attachment geometry across related observed cores, alongside coherent local series within a core. Core novelty alone cannot create missing decoration combinations, and each combination must earn its value from actual feedback rather than a named objective template.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Digest witnesses include an unusual neutral hydrogen-bearing sulfur ring at 0.31554657771518013, an allyl azide at 0.0, an N-hydroxy/trichloromethyl formamide at 0.007693218186208301, and intricately connected unassigned polycycles. Conversely, an N-O-containing isoxazoline scores 0.48839749189747395. The mixture supports contextual chemical scrutiny rather than treating every N-O bond, unusual atom or ring as categorically undesirable.
transferable_gaps.gap: The valid output does not consistently distinguish conventional medicinal structures from unusual bonding and difficult-to-define polycycles.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: A task-agnostic generator would need chemical plausibility that considers complete bond and valence environments, plausible assembly and stereochemical definition, beyond successful SMILES parsing. Any such capability should preserve supported heterocyclic chemistry and be checked against the actual generated structures rather than a blanket functional-group ban.

method_name: Augmented Hill-Climb with a corpus-trained SMILES policy
method_thesis: Train a compact autoregressive SMILES prior solely on the supplied unlabeled corpus, then initialize a fresh policy from that prior for each objective. Use the initial observations and each subsequent scored batch to update only its highest-reward sequences with the Augmented Hill-Climb loss: fit policy log likelihood to frozen-prior log likelihood plus scaled observed reward. Sample complete molecules token by token from the updated policy, canonicalize them, and refill invalid or duplicate proposals by further generation. The corpus supplies language training, never a ranked molecular pool. Elite-conditioned policy updates should shift generation toward new high-scoring molecular combinations quickly enough to improve the benchmark's mean final Top-1. This is a small-budget transfer hypothesis, not a claim that published larger-budget gains carry over. The root uses the current scored batch; randomized historical replay is reserved for the first improvement. The anchor's elite augmented-likelihood mechanism is described by [Thomas et al.](https://link.springer.com/article/10.1186/s13321-022-00646-z).

approach.method_basis: The Parent trains a recurrent SMILES language model on an unlabeled molecular corpus and starts each objective with a fresh policy copied from that frozen prior. Each accepted batch supplies its highest-scoring half, joined by the strongest eligible original strings from a memory of thirty-two earlier elites. Historical fitting weights decrease with previous training exposure while current and historical groups retain their total loss shares. The policy fits weighted squared error toward frozen-prior sequence log likelihood plus sixty times accepted reward, projecting each positive target independently to zero, using bounded clipped Adam updates and retaining the final policy. It then samples complete SMILES directly from the adapted policy and submits the first valid, canonically novel identities in sample order, refilling when necessary and discarding surplus draws.
approach.novelty: Add progressive spacing of repeated molecular cores during admission. The first new molecule with a ring-and-linker core is admitted immediately. Once that core occupies k places in the current batch, its next admission requires k+1 further distinct valid draws of that core; intervening draws are discarded. Other newly encountered cores can therefore reach the same batch, while a dominant core remains admissible and no randomness is added. Earlier siblings diversified retained training memory or balanced choices of breeding parents. This change acts directly on fresh policy samples before oracle submission, leaving both training membership rules and token generation intact. Same-stream admission receipts will show whether additional cores actually reach evaluation. The earlier diversity experiments also warn that spacing a productive family can weaken exploitation.

research_intent.falsifier: The registered admission mechanism is refuted if any open-capacity valid novel draw is admitted with a<k+1, rejected with a==k+1, or uses a core key inconsistent with the declared atom/bond-typed scaffold and acyclic/fallback rule; if counters advance on invalid, duplicate or post-capacity draws; if per-core state crosses suggestions; or if the actual emissions, pending strings or diagnostic comparator introduce an ungenerated molecule or reordered output. At least one eligible repeated-core rejection is required for activated thinning; absence of an opportunity is untested rather than activation. If thinning activates and an alternative first-occurrence core is encountered before completion but is suppressed by core occupancy, the direct core-delivery mechanism is refuted. If no completed batch gains a core over its same-stream first-come comparator, the proposed realized coverage effect is unsupported even when the gate executes correctly. Extra RNG draws, modified upstream learning/memory rules, score use in admission or sourcing a batch from discarded records violate isolation. Failure to complete the frozen evaluation panel or a paired endpoint mean gain below the supplied minimum rejects the utility claim without undoing verified gate execution. Higher refill cost or lower scores despite greater coverage are adverse outcomes to report, not grounds to relax the gate after seeing results.

At the start of each suggest call, create empty suggestion-local dictionaries emitted_core_count and novel_since_core_emission. For an RDKit-valid canonically novel draw, keep the inherited global self.seen exclusion and suggestion-wide batch_seen deduplication: add the identity to batch_seen before any new admission decision, so repeated serializations of a previously thinned draw are also duplicates for the remainder of this suggestion. If output capacity is already full, retain the capacity-discard behavior and do not advance admission state. finding_summary.headline: Core thinning delivered broader molecular batches, but final Top-1 fell despite higher AUC.
finding_summary.insights:
The experiment resolves the delivery question: additional cores already present in fresh policy samples can reach the oracle without losing the first-come batch's core support. That delivery was often unproductive. Of the 242 additional core representatives, only six improved the actual incumbent: four on zaleplon and two on docking. Deco-hop received 116 additional core representatives without an incumbent improvement from any of them. Its previously dominant phenyl/anilinoquinazoline core was evaluated 54 times instead of 160 and reached a lower best score. This is compatible with diluted exploitation, although unscored discarded molecules cannot identify the value of any particular forgone proposal.

Coverage is also a poor predictor of the magnitude of the final change. Sitagliptin gained only seven batch-level cores yet had the largest mean endpoint loss. Admission changes alter later feedback and therefore later generated streams; a same-stream comparison isolates immediate delivery, not the complete search that would have followed different admissions. The higher AUC and lower endpoint further separate earlier progress from the final objective.

The chemical assessment narrows what broader coverage did not repair. Productive functional-group attachment arrangements remain inconsistently preserved, and the many structures with potential stereochemistry still have no specified configurations. Those are open chemical capabilities, not established causes of this score loss. Useful next evidence would need to show that broader admission preserves productive local series or transfers their attachment chemistry, rather than using core count as a proxy for usefulness. The utility claim is rejected while the admission and delivery mechanism is confirmed.
finding_summary.results:
The admission mechanism ran correctly and changed which constitutional cores reached evaluation. Across 435 batches, it rejected 436 eligible repeated-core draws in 167 batches. Comparing each recorded stream with its first ten valid novel structures, actual batches gained cores 159 times and never lost a previously represented core. Mean core count increased from 9.106 to 9.662, delivering 242 additional batch-level core representatives and changing 304 canonical output identities. Mean core concentration fell from 0.133 to 0.110. All state transitions, original-string provenance and paired behavior before the first intervention passed the passive audit.

All fifteen task sessions completed their budgets. Mean final Top-1 fell from 0.522705 to 0.508247, a paired change of -0.014458 against the required +0.002 increase. Seed changes were +0.009826, -0.032176 and -0.021023; population dispersion across seed scores changed from 0.020072 to 0.019593. Task mean changes were -0.014692 for zaleplon, -0.014459 for deco-hop, -0.005454 for median-2 and -0.037685 for sitagliptin; docking decreased by only 0.000000211 near its ceiling. Recorded mean AUC nevertheless rose from 0.405593 to 0.430066, chiefly through earlier progress on docking and zaleplon.

Broader batches required more work. Raw draws increased from 35,568 to 36,880, and batches needing extra sampling increased from 16 to 28. Raw duplication rose from 32.21% to 34.50%, while validity fell from 91.79% to 91.11%. No generation limit was exhausted. Recorded generation time rose from 24.75 to 37.90 seconds across the panel, including 10.38 seconds for core extraction and 0.52 seconds for receipts; the interval gate itself took 0.009 seconds.

finding_summary.headline: Core thinning delivered broader molecular batches, but final Top-1 fell despite higher AUC.
finding_summary.insights:
The experiment resolves the delivery question: additional cores already present in fresh policy samples can reach the oracle without losing the first-come batch's core support. That delivery was often unproductive. Of the 242 additional core representatives, only six improved the actual incumbent: four on zaleplon and two on docking. Deco-hop received 116 additional core representatives without an incumbent improvement from any of them. Its previously dominant phenyl/anilinoquinazoline core was evaluated 54 times instead of 160 and reached a lower best score. This is compatible with diluted exploitation, although unscored discarded molecules cannot identify the value of any particular forgone proposal.

Coverage is also a poor predictor of the magnitude of the final change. Sitagliptin gained only seven batch-level cores yet had the largest mean endpoint loss. Admission changes alter later feedback and therefore later generated streams; a same-stream comparison isolates immediate delivery, not the complete search that would have followed different admissions. The higher AUC and lower endpoint further separate earlier progress from the final objective.

The chemical assessment narrows what broader coverage did not repair. Productive functional-group attachment arrangements remain inconsistently preserved, and the many structures with potential stereochemistry still have no specified configurations. Those are open chemical capabilities, not established causes of this score loss. Useful next evidence would need to show that broader admission preserves productive local series or transfers their attachment chemistry, rather than using core count as a proxy for usefulness. The utility claim is rejected while the admission and delivery mechanism is confirmed.
finding_summary.results:
The admission mechanism ran correctly and changed which constitutional cores reached evaluation. Across 435 batches, it rejected 436 eligible repeated-core draws in 167 batches. Comparing each recorded stream with its first ten valid novel structures, actual batches gained cores 159 times and never lost a previously represented core. Mean core count increased from 9.106 to 9.662, delivering 242 additional batch-level core representatives and changing 304 canonical output identities. Mean core concentration fell from 0.133 to 0.110. All state transitions, original-string provenance and paired behavior before the first intervention passed the passive audit.

All fifteen task sessions completed their budgets. Mean final Top-1 fell from 0.522705 to 0.508247, a paired change of -0.014458 against the required +0.002 increase. Seed changes were +0.009826, -0.032176 and -0.021023; population dispersion across seed scores changed from 0.020072 to 0.019593. Task mean changes were -0.014692 for zaleplon, -0.014459 for deco-hop, -0.005454 for median-2 and -0.037685 for sitagliptin; docking decreased by only 0.000000211 near its ceiling. Recorded mean AUC nevertheless rose from 0.405593 to 0.430066, chiefly through earlier progress on docking and zaleplon.

Broader batches required more work. Raw draws increased from 35,568 to 36,880, and batches needing extra sampling increased from 16 to 28. Raw duplication rose from 32.21% to 34.50%, while validity fell from 91.79% to 91.11%. No generation limit was exhausted. Recorded generation time rose from 24.75 to 37.90 seconds across the panel, including 10.38 seconds for core extraction and 0.52 seconds for receipts; the interval gate itself took 0.009 seconds.

finding_summary.headline: Core thinning delivered broader molecular batches, but final Top-1 fell despite higher AUC.
finding_summary.insights:
The experiment resolves the delivery question: additional cores already present in fresh policy samples can reach the oracle without losing the first-come batch's core support. That delivery was often unproductive. Of the 242 additional core representatives, only six improved the actual incumbent: four on zaleplon and two on docking. Deco-hop received 116 additional core representatives without an incumbent improvement from any of them. Its previously dominant phenyl/anilinoquinazoline core was evaluated 54 times instead of 160 and reached a lower best score. This is compatible with diluted exploitation, although unscored discarded molecules cannot identify the value of any particular forgone proposal.

Coverage is also a poor predictor of the magnitude of the final change. Sitagliptin gained only seven batch-level cores yet had the largest mean endpoint loss. Admission changes alter later feedback and therefore later generated streams; a same-stream comparison isolates immediate delivery, not the complete search that would have followed different admissions. The higher AUC and lower endpoint further separate earlier progress from the final objective.

The chemical assessment narrows what broader coverage did not repair. Productive functional-group attachment arrangements remain inconsistently preserved, and the many structures with potential stereochemistry still have no specified configurations. Those are open chemical capabilities, not established causes of this score loss. Useful next evidence would need to show that broader admission preserves productive local series or transfers their attachment chemistry, rather than using core count as a proxy for usefulness. The utility claim is rejected while the admission and delivery mechanism is confirmed.
finding_summary.results:
The admission mechanism ran correctly and changed which constitutional cores reached evaluation. Across 435 batches, it rejected 436 eligible repeated-core draws in 167 batches. Comparing each recorded stream with its first ten valid novel structures, actual batches gained cores 159 times and never lost a previously represented core. Mean core count increased from 9.106 to 9.662, delivering 242 additional batch-level core representatives and changing 304 canonical output identities. Mean core concentration fell from 0.133 to 0.110. All state transitions, original-string provenance and paired behavior before the first intervention passed the passive audit.

All fifteen task sessions completed their budgets. Mean final Top-1 fell from 0.522705 to 0.508247, a paired change of -0.014458 against the required +0.002 increase. Seed changes were +0.009826, -0.032176 and -0.021023; population dispersion across seed scores changed from 0.020072 to 0.019593. Task mean changes were -0.014692 for zaleplon, -0.014459 for deco-hop, -0.005454 for median-2 and -0.037685 for sitagliptin; docking decreased by only 0.000000211 near its ceiling. Recorded mean AUC nevertheless rose from 0.405593 to 0.430066, chiefly through earlier progress on docking and zaleplon.

Broader batches required more work. Raw draws increased from 35,568 to 36,880, and batches needing extra sampling increased from 16 to 28. Raw duplication rose from 32.21% to 34.50%, while validity fell from 91.79% to 91.11%. No generation limit was exhausted. Recorded generation time rose from 24.75 to 37.90 seconds across the panel, including 10.38 seconds for core extraction and 0.52 seconds for receipts; the interval gate itself took 0.009 seconds.

approach.method_basis: The Parent trains a recurrent SMILES language model on an unlabeled molecular corpus and starts each objective with a fresh policy copied from that frozen prior. Each accepted batch supplies its highest-scoring half, joined by the strongest eligible original strings from a memory of thirty-two earlier elites. Historical fitting weights decrease with previous training exposure while current and historical groups retain their total loss shares. The policy fits weighted squared error toward frozen-prior sequence log likelihood plus sixty times accepted reward, projecting each positive target independently to zero, using bounded clipped Adam updates and retaining the final policy. It then samples complete SMILES directly from the adapted policy and submits the first valid, canonically novel identities in sample order, refilling when necessary and discarding surplus draws.
approach.novelty: Add progressive spacing of repeated molecular cores during admission. The first new molecule with a ring-and-linker core is admitted immediately. Once that core occupies k places in the current batch, its next admission requires k+1 further distinct valid draws of that core; intervening draws are discarded. Other newly encountered cores can therefore reach the same batch, while a dominant core remains admissible and no randomness is added. Earlier siblings diversified retained training memory or balanced choices of breeding parents. This change acts directly on fresh policy samples before oracle submission, leaving both training membership rules and token generation intact. Same-stream admission receipts will show whether additional cores actually reach evaluation. The earlier diversity experiments also warn that spacing a productive family can weaken exploitation.
